project.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

ground_truth.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

parsed_output.evidence: Container run output: '[VULNERABLE] Zip Slip succeeded.  Extraction dir : /tmp/mpxj3475323535743176514tmp  Escaped file : /tmp/mpxj_zipslip_pov_1036016718138.txt  EXIT=0'. The escaped file's canonical path is outside the extraction dir, proving the traversal reaches the FileOutputStream write.
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: On unpatched code the malicious entry '../<marker>.txt' is written outside the temporary extraction directory (into its parent, e.g. /tmp/<marker>.txt); the POV detects the escaped file via canonical-path comparison and exits 0. After a correct patch that rejects or sanitizes traversal entries, the file is never created outside the dir (or extraction throws), and the command exits 1.
parsed_output.notes: The POV compiles only the two standard-library-only project sources (FileHelper.java, InputStreamHelper.java) together with the POV and runs it directly, so it exercises the real vulnerable code without needing a full mvn build. run_pov.sh writes compiled classes to .security-pipeline/pov/classes and cleans up the extracted temp dir and escaped file after each run. Marker filename uses System.nanoTime() to avoid collisions.
parsed_output.regression_hint: A fix should validate that the canonical path of `new File(dir, entry.getName())` is contained within the canonical path of `dir` before writing (reject or skip entries that escape). After that, ZipSlipPov exits non-zero because no file is created in the extraction dir's parent.
parsed_output.summary: Confirmed Zip Slip (CWE-022) path traversal in net.sf.mpxj.common.InputStreamHelper.writeZipStreamToTempDir. processZipStream builds each output file with `new File(dir, entry.getName())` and never verifies the resolved path stays within the temp extraction dir, so a crafted zip entry name containing '../' writes files outside the directory. The POV builds a real zip whose entry is '../<marker>.txt', calls the public method, and confirms the file was written to the parent of the extraction dir.

parsed_output.patch_notes: In processZipStream, after building `File file = new File(dir, entry.getName())`, I added a canonical-path containment check: compute `dir.getCanonicalPath() + File.separator` and reject the entry with an IOException if `file.getCanonicalPath()` does not start with it. This runs before the directory/file branch, so it blocks both `mkdirsQuietly(parent)` and the `FileOutputStream` write paths flagged in the alert traces. Legitimate nested entries still resolve inside the directory and extract normally. The new test InputStreamHelperTest verifies (1) a '../' entry is rejected and no file is written to the temp parent, and (2) a valid nested entry is still extracted. Both tests pass in the project container.
parsed_output.risk_notes: Low risk. The change is a focused guard with no dependency or API changes. Canonical-path resolution requires filesystem access (already the case since entries are written to disk) and appends File.separator to the directory path to prevent sibling-prefix false negatives. Behavior for well-formed archives is unchanged; only entries resolving outside the extraction directory now fail fast with an IOException, which callers of writeZipStreamToTempDir already handle as an IOException.
parsed_output.summary: Fixed a Zip Slip (CWE-022) path traversal in InputStreamHelper.processZipStream. Each zip entry's output file is now validated so its canonical path stays within the temp extraction directory; entries that escape (e.g. names containing '../') throw an IOException before any file is created or written. Added a JUnit regression test.

parsed_output.diff_review: patch_only.diff touches two files. (1) InputStreamHelper.java: after `File file = new File(dir, entry.getName())`, it computes `dir.getCanonicalPath() + File.separator` and throws IOException if `file.getCanonicalPath()` does not start with it. The guard is correctly placed before both the directory branch (mkdirsQuietly) and the FileOutputStream write path, covering all three alert traces (lines 129, 136/parent, 139/file). Appending File.separator correctly prevents sibling-prefix false negatives (e.g. dir vs dir-evil). Legitimate nested entries (nested/data.txt) still resolve inside dir and extract normally. IOException is already the declared/handled exception type for this method, so no new failure surface for callers. (2) Adds a new JUnit test InputStreamHelperTest.java exercising both rejection and valid-entry paths — test-only, does not weaken the fix. pov.diff only adds POV harness files and does not modify project source; the patcher did not alter or disable the POV. No unrelated or broad behavior changes.
parsed_output.pov_result: Reran the POV via the Docker wrapper. Output: "[NOT VULNERABLE] Extraction rejected the traversal entry: java.io.IOException: Zip entry is outside of the target directory: ../mpxj_zipslip_pov_1174888510202.txt" with EXIT=1. The traversal no longer writes outside the extraction dir; the malicious entry is rejected before any file is created. Confirmed vulnerable before patch per orchestrator log (exit 0, escaped file in /tmp).
parsed_output.regression_result: Reran `mvn -B -Dtest=InputStreamHelperTest test` via the Docker wrapper: Tests run: 2, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0, BUILD SUCCESS. Both the traversal-rejection and valid-nested-entry tests pass, confirming the fix blocks the attack while preserving legitimate extraction.
parsed_output.summary: The patch adds a canonical-path containment check in InputStreamHelper.processZipStream that rejects zip entries resolving outside the temp extraction directory, fixing the Zip Slip (CWE-022) path traversal. It is minimal and correct; the original POV no longer reproduces and regression tests pass.
